headline: Batch correction, imputation and splicing benchmarks advance single-cell omics analysis
label: Single Cell Transcriptomic Analysis Methods
summary: Preprints and papers target batch effects, missing values and transcript assembly that constrain single-cell and proteomic data interpretation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is correcting or modeling technical structure before biological inference. Several items address batch effects and missing values: omicsGMF unifies batch correction, imputation and dimensionality reduction for bulk and single-cell proteomics, NMFBatch combines non-negative matrix factorization with generalized additive models, and GIRAFI imputes sparse single-cell proteomics using prior-knowledge protein neighborhoods. COTAN models zero counts directly for UMI droplet scRNA-seq instead of log-normalizing. A benchmark of six alternative splicing methods on single-cell RNA-seq extends this methodological focus to isoform-level analysis. Other items, including RB-dRNAseq, StringTie3 and SpatialArtifacts, address sequencing multiplexing, transcript assembly and tissue artifacts, respectively, and are not part of the same thread.
